title: Normalized pulse-area augmentation worsened BIDMC respiratory-rate estimates and gave inconclusive primary improvement in independent CapnoBase recordings
abstract: We tested respiratory modulation of beat-normalized PPG contour area beyond intensity, amplitude and interval spectra. Among prespecified positive area weights, BIDMC development selected0.25, although all positive weights worsened participant-macro mean absolute error. At that frozen weight, error rose from4.056 to4.305 breaths/min in53 BIDMC recordings. In42 independent CapnoBase recordings,64-second-window error decreased from2.490 to2.049 breaths/min, but the paired participant-bootstrap95% interval for candidate-minus-baseline error was−1.159 to0.043. Thus primary external superiority was not established. A prespecified32-second sensitivity was favorable; temporal-shape shuffle comparisons were inconclusive. These results do not establish a consistently transferable improvement, a novel physiological mechanism, or clinical utility. We provide frozen choices, input hashes, code, window-level results, self-checks and exact clean reruns.
